inline_comments.comment: `useHtmlLabels` is passed as the `addBackground` argument to `createLabel` here and at lines 120, 143, and 167. These are semantically different things: `useHtmlLabels` is `true` whenever HTML rendering is enabled (a common default), while `addBackground` controls whether the `labelBkg` CSS class is applied to the label container div. The net effect is that all four terminal labels (startLabelLeft, startLabelRight, endLabelLeft, endLabelRight) will silently receive a background box whenever HTML labels are active — which is almost certainly unintentional. The main edge label at line 58 uses `createText` with an explicit `addSvgBackground: true`; if terminal labels are not meant to have backgrounds, this argument should be `false` (or a dedicated flag derived from `edge` properties).

`style.replace('color:', 'fill:')` is called without a null/undefined guard in the SVG (non-HTML) label path. `style` can be `undefined` — e.g., when `rectWithTitle.ts` passes `node.labelStyle` and the node has no style. The HTML-label branch just above correctly guards with `style ? style.replace('fill:', 'color:') : style` (line 109). The same guard is missing here, so calling this function with an undefined style while `htmlLabels` is disabled will throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')`. The same issue exists at line 109 of `packages/mermaid/src/dagre-wrapper/createLabel.js`.

The log level was changed from `log.debug` to `log.info` for what is a raw diagnostic dump of `vertexText`. Per project conventions, development debugging statements should use `log.debug()` or `log.trace()`, not `log.info()`. Also, string concatenation should be replaced with a template literal: `log.debug(`vertexText ${vertexText}`)`. The same issue exists at line 97 of `packages/mermaid/src/dagre-wrapper/createLabel.js`.

`createLabel` is an `async` function that now returns a `Promise<SVGForeignObjectElement>` (including the new measurement logic), but `getClusterTitleWidth` is synchronous and does not `await` it. The `label` variable receives a `Promise`, not a DOM element, so `label.getBBox()` will throw at runtime whenever the HTML-label path is taken. This call site needs to be made `async` and the call must be `await`-ed, or callers of `getClusterTitleWidth` need to be updated accordingly. (This was a latent issue, but the new `addHtmlLabel` implementation — which now does real async work to measure bbox — makes it an active runtime defect.)

The changeset is classified as `patch` with a `fix:` prefix, but the PR adds user-visible new features to `createLabel` paths: KaTeX rendering support and FontAwesome iconpack resolution. Per project rules, changesets that add features should be `minor`. Additionally, the description 'no markdown-specific changes' is inaccurate — KaTeX is a markdown/math feature, and the icon replacement logic is new functionality in this code path.

`DEFAULT_WRAPPING_WIDTH`, `getWrappingWidth()`, and `addHtmlLabel()` are now defined identically in both `packages/mermaid/src/dagre-wrapper/createLabel.js` and `packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/rendering-elements/createLabel.js`. This reintroduces the duplication the PR aimed to eliminate. Consider extracting the shared `addHtmlLabel` implementation (and its dependencies) into `labelImageUtils.ts` or a new shared module, then importing it in both places.

general_comments.comment: The PR description states the goal is to reduce duplication between label rendering paths, but the actual implementation widens the duplication: `addHtmlLabel`, `DEFAULT_WRAPPING_WIDTH`, and `getWrappingWidth` are now defined twice — nearly identically — in both `dagre-wrapper/createLabel.js` and `rendering-util/rendering-elements/createLabel.js`. Any future fix to one copy (e.g., the `try/finally` leak fix, the `log.debug` correction, a behaviour tweak to wrapping logic) must be manually replicated in the other. The path to the stated goal of a unified pipeline would be to have one of the two `createLabel.js` files re-export or import from the other, or to lift shared logic into the already-created `labelImageUtils.ts`.

The removed `div.style('padding-right', '1px')` line in `rendering-util/rendering-elements/createLabel.js` had a comment ('Fix for firefox') in the original code. Silently dropping it as part of a style cleanup introduces a potential rendering regression in Firefox without an explanation or a test that would catch it. If the padding is no longer needed, a comment explaining why should be in the PR description or a code comment.
